page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: page number at the head; a woodcut diagram of a circle with an inscribed triangle (vertices C, A, B, and a centre point) above one column of text. Right page: only a narrow strip of its left margin notes at the scan edge; its body text is not on the scan.

main_text.p: V. Adumbrantur autem & demonstrantur hoc Schemate, varia omnino in Deo mysteria summa, & quidem

1. Vnitas & communitas Essentiæ divinæ communi centro peripheriæ & Arearum Trianguli; ita ut tres numero distincti anguli unam numero aream, radii unum centrum, anguli unam peripheriam continent, sic tres personæ unam numero essentiam habent in Deo.
2. Trinitas[?] personarum etiam demonstratur tribus angulis A, B, C.
a. Ut nec pauciores nec plures anguli sunt in Triangulo, ita tres personæ, non plures nec pauciores sunt in unitate Essentiæ Dei.

b. Ut tres anguli figuram Trianguli con-[right page margin notes, cut off at scan edge: clu / per / &u / gul / lati / liur / ficq / d / latio / 3- / am t / later / quæl / refpe / quili / tinet / tegra / ß. / æqual / &per / γ. / peripl / essent]

page.notes: The diagram is a circle with an inscribed triangle whose corners are labelled C (top), A (lower left) and B (lower right); a centre point is joined to all three corners. The letters A, B, C in the diagram are printed in the figure. The faint mirrored text at the top of the left page is show-through and is left out. The right-hand strip is cut off at the scan edge, so its notes are only partly legible and are given as fragments. The first word of paragraph 2 is faint; "Trinitas" is a likely reading. The text continues on the next page after "con-"; the catchword "clu-" is printed at the foot right.
